traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Aspleniaceae and the families the Library joins to it (Thelypteridaceae, Blechnaceae, Athyriaceae, Woodsiaceae, Cystopteridaceae, Onocleaceae, Diplaziopsidaceae): Asplenium, the largest, fronds mostly alike, simple to many times pinnate, sori single, long and narrow along a vein, the indusium a flap fixed along the vein's side; Blechnaceae and Athyriaceae sori long, beside the midrib or along one side of a vein, with flaps; Thelypteridaceae sori round to oblong, indusium present or not; Woodsia and Cystopteris round sori with basal or hood-like indusia; Blechnum and Onoclea fronds dimorphic. Linear sori are the usual state, as Asplenium, Blechnum and the lady ferns hold most of the Library's species.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 118, 120, family Aspleniaceae: leaf venation pinnate (or forking, free), usually; read as {"pinnate": "usually"}.

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 118, 120, family Aspleniaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 118, 120, family Aspleniaceae: rhizome habit short_creeping (creeping, climbing, ascending or suberect), often; read as {"short_creeping": "often"}.
